title: Click Guard → One device, many IPs

steps.caption: Traffic signals
steps.narration: A browser fingerprint lets Click Guard recognise a device even when its IP changes. Here's what that looks like.

steps.caption: Same device, different IPs
steps.narration: This address was flagged: Same device fingerprint seen from different IPs.

steps.caption: Its neighbour
steps.narration: The address next to it was blocked by hand after a look at its visits.

steps.caption: Search the range
steps.narration: Search for the start of the range and both addresses come up.

steps.caption: Same device, browser, system
steps.narration: Same device type, same browser, same operating system, same page, from two IPs.

steps.caption: Tools
steps.narration: The fingerprint comes from the tracking code on your pages, under Tools.

steps.caption: What the code captures
steps.narration: It captures the device fingerprint, the IP, the browser and the screen size on each page load.

steps.caption: Google Ads script
steps.narration: Under Google Ads script, the rule is listed with the others.

steps.caption: The rule
steps.narration: Same device fingerprint appearing from different IPs.

steps.caption: More about exclusions and limits
steps.narration: Open More about exclusions and limits.

steps.caption: A signal, not proof
steps.narration: Smarter than IP alone, as the page says, but a signal can flag a real visitor, so review before you block.

steps.caption: Menu: Traffic signals
steps.narration: The flagged addresses are under Traffic signals, in Click Guard.

youtube.title: How Click Guard spots one device on many IPs | ConstructHUB
youtube.description: How Click Guard in ConstructHUB uses a browser fingerprint to notice the same device coming back from different IP addresses. You will see the flag on Blocked IPs, the matching visits in the Clicks report, and where the tracking code captures the fingerprint.
